why: A = the conjunction of 50 theorems at universe 0. A_to_B: the main conjunct theorem_15_4_1 gives IsCanonicalFor of canonicalOrientation only under three hypotheses B does not have: sc-smooth bump functions (AdmitsBumpFunctions), tame germ data (IsScFredholmSectionTame f), and a constant index n on supp(Λ∘f); B has no index hypothesis at all. B's (a), local kernel structures (exists_kernelBranching), also needs hft. B_to_A: the main conjunct does not presuppose that Θ is branched, while B does. B then yields only some orientation T that agrees with the kernel sums at smooth points. IsCanonicalFor additionally needs continuity of the frames along the sheets and sheet dimension n; these are the item theorems KernelBranching.framesContinuous and KernelBranching.dim_eq_of_isIndexAt, the substance of Theorem 15.4.1, and would have to be re-proved. The remaining conjuncts are transfer lemmas, pull-back statements and examples.
overlap: No direction proved, so #rt_overlap was not run.

main.note: A-main has extra hypotheses: hbump, hft and a constant index on the support. B has an extra presupposition (Θ branched) and draws its conclusion for any index profile. B_to_A would need re-proving the frame-continuity and dimension lemmas.
